help_modal.ally_betray: Betray your ally, ending the alliance, halting trade, and weakening your defense. Trading between you is paused for 5 minutes (or until you become allies again) and others may stop trading too. And unless the other player was a traitor themselves, you'll be marked a traitor for 30 seconds. During this time an icon will be above your name and you will have a 50% defense debuff. Barons are less likely to ally with you and players will think twice before doing so.
help_modal.ally_donate: Donate some of your troops to your ally. Used when they're low on troops and are being attacked, or when they need that extra power to crush an enemy.
help_modal.ally_donate_gold: Donate some of your gold to your ally. Used when they're low on gold and need it for buildings, or when your team member is saving for a Stargate or a warhead.
help_modal.build_atom_desc: Small explosive bomb that destroys territory, buildings, ships and fleets. Spawns from the nearest ready Stargate with the target in range (the Hegemon fires it from the Dark Star itself) and lands in the area you first clicked to build it. It cannot harm anything inside another player's Shield Array, though it still clears the ground around it.
help_modal.build_city_desc: Increases your max population. Useful when you can't expand your territory or you're about to hit your population limit.
help_modal.build_defense_desc: Increases defenses around nearby borders, which show a checkered pattern. Attacks from enemies are slower and have more casualties.
help_modal.build_factory_desc: Automatically lays straight trade lanes to nearby cities, spaceports and other factories, and can also link up with friendly neighbors. Trains spawn regularly and give you a fixed amount of gold for each building they visit along the route, with extra gold for visiting your neighbors' buildings.
help_modal.build_hydrogen_desc: Large explosive bomb. Spawns from the nearest ready Stargate with the target in range (the Hegemon fires it from the Dark Star itself) and lands in the area you first clicked to build it. It cannot harm anything inside another player's Shield Array, though it still clears the ground around it.
help_modal.build_menu_desc: Build these or see how many of each you already build:
help_modal.build_port_desc: Can be built anywhere in your territory; its freighters put to space at the nearest deep space, crawling overland at half speed on the way. Allows building Destroyers. Automatically sends freighters between spaceports of your country and other countries (except when trade is stopped), giving gold to both sides. Trade with a player stops automatically when you attack or are attacked by a player. It resumes after 5 minutes or if you become allies. You can manually toggle trading with "Stop trading" or "Start trading".
help_modal.build_shield_array_desc: Projects a shield 35 tiles around it. No other player's missile can harm anything inside the shield, the Hegemon's included; a blast still clears everything around it. The Hegemon's strikes pass through. One level only, no upgrades.
help_modal.build_stargate_desc: Fires troops (your attack ratio) at any tile in range that is not yours. The shot lands and fights like a fleet landing, and the land is kept; it may land on the Dark Star. Also the launcher for warheads. Costs {cost} gold, new or per upgrade, with no level cap: {base} tiles of range at level 1 and +{per} per level. One shot, then a {reload} second reload.
help_modal.build_warship_desc: Patrols an area, capturing enemy freighters and destroying their fleets and Destroyers. Launches from the harbour of your nearest Spaceport on that body of space and patrols the area you first clicked. Control Destroyers by attack-clicking them (see Attack under Hotkeys), then attack-clicking where they should go. They level up (max level 3) by capturing freighters and destroying fleets and Destroyers; each level adds damage and health.
help_modal.community_desc: Found a bug, or something troubleshooting did not fix? Tell us on the Discord server, or write to us.

help_modal.icon_desc: Examples of some of the ingame icons you will encounter and what they mean:
help_modal.icon_embargo: Dollar stop sign - Embargo. This player has stopped trading with you automatically or manually.
help_modal.icon_request: Envelope - Alliance request. This player has sent you an alliance request.
help_modal.icon_traitor: Broken shield - Traitor. This player attacked an ally.
help_modal.in_game_tutorial_desc: Learn by playing: a solo game with a step-by-step guide that walks you through spawning, attacking, building and warheads.
help_modal.info_alliance: Send an alliance request to the player. Allies can share resources and troops, but can't attack each other.
help_modal.info_ally_desc: When you ally with a player, the following new icons become available:
help_modal.info_chat: Send a quick chat message to the player. Select a Category, a Phrase, and if the phrase contains [P1] select a Player name to replace it with. Hit Send.
help_modal.info_emoji: Send an emoji to the player.
help_modal.info_enemy_desc: Contains information such as the selected player's name, gold, troops, stopped trading with you, nukes sent to you, and if the player is a traitor. Stopped trading means you won't receive gold from them and they won't sent you gold via freighters. Manually (if the player clicked "Stop trading", which lasts until you both click "Start trading") or automatically (if you betrayed your alliance, which lasts until you become allies again or after 5 minutes). Traitor displays Yes for 30 seconds when the player betrayed and attacked a player who was in an alliance with them. The icons below represent the following interactions:
help_modal.info_target: Place a target mark on the player, marking it for all allies, used to coordinate attacks.
help_modal.info_trade: Use "Stop trading" to stop giving the player gold and receiving their gold via freighters. If you both click "Start trading" it will start again.
help_modal.option_pause: Pause/Unpause the game - Unavailable in public games.
help_modal.option_settings: Settings - Open the settings menu. Inside you can toggle things like Alternate view, Emojis, Dark Mode, Hidden names, action on left click and more.
help_modal.option_speed: Speed - Adjust the game speed. Unavailable in public games.
help_modal.option_timer: Timer - Time passed since the start of the game.
help_modal.radial_boat: Send a fleet to attack at the selected location. Only available if your territory touches deep space.
help_modal.radial_desc: Right clicking (or touch on mobile) opens the Radial menu. Right click outside it to close it. From the menu you can:
help_modal.radial_donate_gold: Opens the gold donation slider menu so you can quickly send allies gold.
help_modal.radial_donate_troops: Donate troops equivalent to your attack ratio slider percentage to the ally you opened the radial menu on.
help_modal.radial_reinforce: Reinforce the throne: send troops equal to your attack ratio to the Hegemon. While someone is invading the Dark Star, they join the counter-attack at once.
help_modal.rules_arsenal_1: Stargate: {gateCost} gold, new or per upgrade, no level cap. It fires troops (your attack ratio) at any tile that is not yours within its range: {gateBase} tiles at level 1, +{gatePer} per level. The shot lands and fights like a fleet landing and the land is kept. One shot, then a {gateReload} second reload. A shot may target the Dark Star, subject to the invader rule, and can be recalled in flight.
help_modal.rules_arsenal_2: Warheads launch from the nearest ready Stargate whose range covers the target and spend that gate's charge: the Nuclear Warhead costs {nukeCost} gold, the Antimatter Warhead {hCost}. The Hegemon fires warheads from the centre of the Dark Star without a gate.
help_modal.rules_arsenal_3: Punitive strikes: launching a warhead flags the gate for {flag} seconds. The Hegemon may answer by clicking the gate. Every living challenger, the launcher included, is levied {levyN}% (Nuclear) or {levyA}% (Antimatter) of the troops they have at home, and the levy lands on the gate as a strike that captures it and razes everything within {pRadius} tiles. No tyranny penalty, no recall. When nothing in reach is left it halts for {halt} seconds, then pops: the gate and every captured structure are destroyed and the troops left over are burnt. A player already under a strike cannot be flagged again until it ends.
help_modal.rules_arsenal_4: Shield Array: {shieldCost} gold, one level, a {shieldR} tile radius. No other player's warhead can harm anything inside it, the Hegemon's included; the blast still clears the ground outside the perimeter. Strikes pass through. It protects nothing while under construction, shields whoever captures it, and does not keep out its owner's own warheads.
help_modal.rules_domain_1: The Dark Star is a solid disc at the centre of every map, separated from the rest by a ring of deep space, the moat. It is the only land the Hegemon can ever own.
help_modal.rules_domain_2: Nothing can be built on Dark Star tiles, by anyone, ever. The Hegemon has no structures of its own anywhere.
help_modal.rules_domain_3: Warheads do nothing to Dark Star tiles. The only way to take them is to land troops: by fleet across the moat, or by a Stargate shot. Taking a tile from the Hegemon costs the attacker more troops and more time than an ordinary conquest.
help_modal.rules_domain_4: Holding Dark Star tiles gives a challenger nothing: no troop capacity, no income. Losing them costs the Hegemon a fixed share of its troops per tile; otherwise its strength does not depend on how much of the disc it holds.
help_modal.rules_gift_1: The Hegemon may build or upgrade any challenger structure on any challenger's land, paying from its own gold. The structure belongs to the host from the moment it is placed and cannot be refused.
help_modal.rules_gift_2: Spaceports are placed anywhere in your territory, like a city. A port's harbour is the nearest deep space reachable over land: freighters crawl overland at half speed to it and travel at full speed across space, and Destroyers launch from and repair at a harbour.
help_modal.rules_gift_3: Trade lanes between stations are straight lines, in the simulation as well as on screen. A line that crosses void, or deep space wider than a strait, does not connect.
help_modal.rules_hegemon_1: The Hegemon starts with a full pool of troops sized from the map ({ceiling}% of what one player owning every land tile could field). The pool refills at a flat rate, empty to full in {refill} minutes, whatever its territory.
help_modal.rules_hegemon_2: Its gold is a shadow tax: every tick it earns {tax}% of everything the challengers earned that tick. Nothing is deducted from anyone.
help_modal.rules_hegemon_3: It cannot expand: land it takes beyond the Dark Star is razed, not kept. It retakes lost Dark Star tiles by ordinary attack.
help_modal.rules_hegemon_4: It cannot ally with anyone and can only be eliminated by invasion. Its tools are the strike, the punitive strike, gifts, troop donations to any challenger, Destroyers in the moat, and warheads fired from the centre of the Dark Star at the normal price with no launcher and no reload.
help_modal.rules_hegemon_5: An AI Hegemon defends the disc; strikes the challenger with the largest troop capacity once its own pool has sat at {leveller}% or more for a minute and that challenger's capacity is at least {threat}% of its ceiling; punishes every flagged Stargate launch except from very small players; and once an invader holds {laststand}% of the disc, sends everything above a {reserve}% reserve after them until they are evicted.
help_modal.rules_intro: Under a Dark Star is an asymmetric round. One player, the Hegemon, holds the Dark Star at the centre of the map and cannot expand; everyone else is a challenger who grows across the galaxy and tries to overthrow them. The numbers below are the current defaults.
help_modal.rules_invasion_1: Only one challenger at a time may hold Dark Star tiles: the invader. The slot is claimed when a fleet or Stargate shot lands on the disc and held for as long as the invader holds any tile there. Anyone else's fleet or shot bound for the disc turns back the moment the slot is taken, troops home.
help_modal.rules_invasion_2: A stalled invasion fights back. If the invader has gained no Dark Star tile for {stall} seconds, all of the Hegemon's troop income is sent against them automatically until they are evicted, for a human or an AI Hegemon alike. A sliver of the disc cannot be sat on.
help_modal.rules_invasion_3: There is no cooldown: an evicted challenger may land again as soon as the slot is free.
help_modal.rules_invasion_4: Anyone may reinforce the throne: donate troops to the Hegemon while its pool has room, with no alliance needed and the lobby's donation setting ignored. While someone is invading, every troop donated joins the counter-attack against them at once. Nobody may donate to the invader.
help_modal.rules_invasion_5: Evicting an invader is ordinary combat. Tyranny does not apply, so a challenger whose homeland is gone can be eliminated on the Dark Star.
help_modal.rules_round_1: A round ends in exactly two ways: the Hegemon is eliminated, or the timer runs out ({minutes} minutes by default). There is no victory by owning a share of the map.
help_modal.rules_round_2: The Hegemon is eliminated when it owns no tiles. The challenger whose attack takes its last tile wins the round and is the Hegemon of the next one.
help_modal.rules_round_3: If the timer runs out with the Hegemon still holding any tile, the Hegemon wins and keeps the throne.
help_modal.rules_round_4: If no human holds the throne, an AI Hegemon plays it. This is also how a solo game works unless you choose to play as the Hegemon yourself.
help_modal.rules_round_5: At the start of a round every challenger is launched from the Dark Star to its chosen spawn. Nothing moves and the clock holds until the last one has landed; spawn protection starts at the landing.
help_modal.rules_round_6: A challenger who loses all territory is out of the round and may spectate or leave. Only a challenger can eliminate a challenger: the Hegemon never can.
help_modal.rules_strike_1: The strike is the Hegemon's attack. It picks any challenger tile and sends a share of its pool; the strike flies visibly from the centre of the Dark Star on a warhead's arc, taking longer the further it goes. On landing it takes the tile and fights outward like a landing.
help_modal.rules_strike_2: Razing is expensive: each tile costs the strike {raze} times the troops and takes {raze} times as long as an ordinary conquest. One live strike per target at a time, any number of targets.
help_modal.rules_strike_3: Tyranny: the troop cost is multiplied by a penalty that depends only on the target's share of the map's land (Dark Star tiles excluded). No penalty at {free}% and above; the multiplier rises without limit below that; at {floor}% and below a player cannot be struck at all, and a strike that razes its target down to that floor ends. The Hegemon can therefore never eliminate anyone.
help_modal.rules_strike_4: The land a strike holds is its bubble. Only the struck player may attack it: use Counter-attack, or click the bubble. It is defended by the strike's own troops, never the Dark Star's, so every tile retaken costs the strike. Structures the bubble rolls over are captured and are destroyed when it pops unless their tile is retaken first.
help_modal.rules_strike_5: A strike ends when its troops are spent, nothing is left in reach, the target is at the tyranny floor, it is recalled, or the Hegemon falls. Its bubble then pops: the land becomes neutral for anyone to take. A recall in flight brings the troops home whole; a recall on the ground pays the usual retreat loss.
help_modal.rules_throne_1: Public lobbies are thrones: named lobbies that run rounds back to back. A throne is FFA, team or special for life. The home page shows the throne starting soonest in each mode; the lobby browser lists every throne under Free for all, Teams or Special, with Watch to spectate a running round.
help_modal.rules_throne_2: After a round the winner has {window} seconds to pick the next map (on a special throne, up to two rule modifiers) and to keep the throne or step down. No answer: a random map, and the winner keeps the throne.
help_modal.rules_throne_3: An open seat is first come, first served: claim it in the lobby, or give it up before the start. If nobody holds it, the AI Hegemon plays. A round needs two humans to start, the Hegemon included.
help_modal.rules_throne_4: A reign counts consecutive rounds held on the same throne: a slayer starts at 1 and each timer win adds one. On a team throne the seat goes to the player who landed the killing blow, not to the team.
help_modal.rules_throne_5: In a private lobby the creator seats the Hegemon by clicking a player's crown. New Lobby from the win screen carries the settings over and seats the winner as they arrive.
help_modal.troubleshooting_desc: If you experience performance issues, crashes, or other problems while playing Under a Dark Star, please visit our Troubleshooting page for help diagnosing and fixing common issues:
help_modal.ui_attack_ratio: Attack ratio - The amount of troops that will be used when you attack. You can adjust the attack ratio using the slider. Having more attacking troops than defending troops will make you lose fewer troops in the attack, while having less will increase the damage dealt to your attacking troops. The effect doesn't go beyond ratios of 2:1.
help_modal.ui_control_desc: The control panel contains the following elements:
help_modal.ui_events_alliance: Alliance - Alliance requests can be accepted or rejected. Allies can share resources and troops, but can't attack each other. Clicking Focus moves the view to the player who sent the request.
help_modal.ui_events_attack: Attacks - Incoming attacks and your outgoing attacks are shown. Click the message to center the view on the attack, warhead or fleet. You can retreat troops by clicking the red X button. This will cost the lives of 25% of your attacking troops. If you recall a fleet, it returns to its starting point and will attack there if the land has been captured since. Warheads can't be recalled once launched; gate shots and strikes can.
help_modal.ui_events_desc: The Event panel displays the latest events, requests and Quick Chat messages. Some examples are:
help_modal.ui_events_quickchat: Quick Chat - You can see sent and received chat messages here. Send a message to a player by clicking the Quick Chat icon in their Info menu.
help_modal.ui_gold: Gold - The amount of gold you have and the rate at which you gain it.
help_modal.ui_leaderboard_desc: Shows the top players of the game and their names, % owned land, gold and troops. Using Show All shows all players in the game. If you don't want to see the leaderboard, click Hide.
help_modal.ui_options_desc: The following elements can be found inside:
help_modal.ui_playeroverlay_desc: When you hover over a country, the Player info overlay appears. It shows the player type (Human, Lord, or Baron), a Lord's attitude toward you (Hostile to Friendly), defending troops, gold, and the number of Warships and buildings they have.

step.alliance_info: Allies can't attack each other. You can break an alliance at any time — but doing so marks you as a traitor.
step.attack_nations: Lords have cut you off from the Barons. Attack a neighboring Lord instead — they're stronger than Barons, so bring plenty of troops. The nearest ones are marked with a target. Conquer them until you have {cost} gold for a City.
step.attack_ratio: The attack ratio bar sets how many of your troops are sent out with each attack. Drag the slider to adjust it.
step.attack_wilderness: The pulsing ring marks your territory. Click on the unclaimed land next to it to attack and expand.
step.buy_city: You can afford a City! Press {key} (or click the City icon under the control panel), then click your territory to place it. Cities raise your max troops.
step.buy_defense_post: Now build a Defense Post: press {key}, then click your territory near a border. Attacks on the land around it are much slower and cost the enemy far more troops.
step.buy_factory: Now build a Factory: press {key}, then click your territory to place it.
step.buy_port: Next, build a Spaceport: press {key}, then click anywhere in your territory to place it. Its ships put to space at the nearest deep space.
step.buy_stargate: Now build a Stargate: press {key}, then click your territory to place it. A gate fires your troops through space at any tile in its range, and is also your warhead launcher.
step.buy_warship: Now build a Destroyer: press {key}, then click deep space near your spaceport. Destroyers capture freighters and guard your space.
step.capture_tribes: Capturing Barons is a great way to earn gold — the nearest ones are marked with a target on the map. Conquer them until you have {cost} gold for a City.
step.dark_star: The disc at the centre of the map is the Dark Star, held by the Hegemon. The round ends when the Hegemon is eliminated or the timer runs out, and whoever takes its last tile wins and holds the throne next round. Build up first: it is far stronger than it looks.
step.earn_gold: Attack neighbors to steal their land, conquer them to take their gold. You need {cost} for a {unit}.
step.factory_info: Factories are joined to cities and other factories by straight trade lanes, and spawn trains that grant gold.
step.fire_gate: Your gate is ready! Right-click a tile in its range that is not yours, open the stargate menu and pick the sword, Gate shot. The shot lands and fights like a fleet, and the land is kept.
step.gate_loading: Your Stargate is building or reloading. A shot can be fired once it is ready.
step.invade_info_slot: To win, land on the Dark Star by fleet across the moat or by gate shot. Only one invader at a time may hold tiles there, and if your advance stalls for {stall} seconds the throne's whole income is sent against you.
step.invade_info_win: Take the Hegemon's last tile and you win the round and the throne. Other players can reinforce the throne with troops, so bring more than you think you need.
step.no_coast: You have no coastline yet. Reaching deep space matters — it lets you send fleets and launch destroyers. Spaceports work anywhere, but their freighters crawl overland until they reach it. Expand your territory until it touches deep space.
step.port_info_ships: Spaceports send out freighters, which earn you gold.
step.port_info_warships: Spaceports also let you launch destroyers.
step.propose_alliance: Lords make strong allies. Right-click the Lord marked with a target and propose an alliance.
step.send_boat: Fleets carry your troops across deep space. Right-click enemy territory on the far side of deep space to open the radial menu, then select the fleet.
step.shield_info: Shield Array: a dome of {shield} tiles that no other player's warhead can harm the inside of, the Hegemon's included. The blast still clears the ground outside it, and the Hegemon's strikes pass through.
step.spawn: Click anywhere on the map to pick where you spawn.
step.spawn_wait: Spot picked! You can still move it until the timer runs out — the game starts then.
step.strike_info: The Hegemon cannot expand, but it can strike: a strike flies from the Dark Star, lands on your land and razes it. The land it holds is its bubble.
step.strike_info_counter: Only you can fight a bubble: use Counter-attack in the attacks panel, or click the bubble. Every tile you retake costs the strike troops, and it can never eliminate you.
step.traitor_info: Traitors get a large defense debuff for 30 seconds, so be careful.
step.troop_rate: This is your troop growth rate. Growth slows down and turns orange once your troops approach half of your max.
step.troops: Keep an eye on your troop count. Attacking with too few troops leaves you weak — let them regrow between attacks.
step.warhead_info_launch: Nuclear and Antimatter Warheads launch from a ready gate whose range covers the target.
step.warhead_info_punish: A launch flags the gate for {flag} seconds: the Hegemon may answer with a punitive strike, paid for by a levy on every player's troops, yours included.

step_touch.attack_wilderness: The pulsing ring marks your territory. Tap the unclaimed land next to it, then tap the sword in the middle of the menu to attack.
step_touch.buy_city: You can afford a City! Tap your territory, open the wrench (Build) menu and pick City. Cities raise your max troops.
step_touch.buy_defense_post: Now build a Defense Post: tap your territory near a border, open the wrench menu and pick Defense Post. Attacks on the land around it are much slower and cost the enemy far more troops.
step_touch.buy_factory: Now build a Factory: tap your territory, open the wrench menu and pick Factory.
step_touch.buy_port: Next, build a Spaceport: tap anywhere in your territory, open the wrench menu and pick Spaceport.
step_touch.buy_stargate: Now build a Stargate: tap your territory, open the wrench menu and pick Stargate. A gate fires your troops through space at any tile in its range, and is also your warhead launcher.
step_touch.buy_warship: Now build a Destroyer: tap deep space near your spaceport, open the stargate menu and pick Destroyer. Destroyers capture freighters and guard your space.
step_touch.fire_gate: Your gate is ready! Tap a tile in its range that is not yours, open the stargate menu and pick the sword, Gate shot. The shot lands and fights like a fleet, and the land is kept.
step_touch.propose_alliance: Lords make strong allies. Tap the Lord marked with a target, then tap the handshake to propose an alliance.
